newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Woman in arson attack at U.S. Moscow embassy.
newsitem.headline: Woman in arson attack at U.S. Moscow embassy.

text.p: A woman arsonist escaped after starting a small fire in the consular section of the U.S. embassy in Moscow on Thursday by igniting petrol, an embassy spokesman said. There were no casualties.
Embassy spokesman Richard Hoagland said the fire was quickly put out. Damage was minor, caused mainly by smoke and water from sprinklers which were triggered automatically.
He said the woman had been carrying the petrol in a plastic bag and poured it over one of two embassy guards, both Americans, as she tried to enter the consulate.
He escaped before she could set him alight but the guards were unable to prevent her starting a small blaze in the entrance to the consular section.
"The woman disappeared in the confusion," Hoagland said.
He declined to say if security had been tightened after the incident, saying only: "The embassy always maintains adequate security."
Hoagland said the woman's identity and her motive for the attack were unknown. Russian firefighters responded quickly but the fire was dealt with before they reached the scene.
"It is too early to estimate the cost of the damage," he said.
Unknown assailants fired a rocket-propelled grenade at the huge Stalin-era building embassy building, on a busy road in central Moscow, on September 13 last year.
No motive was known for that attack, in which no one was hurt and the assailants escaped into the busy traffic.
